spatial_claims.claim: AB is a line segment divided at point C with AC > CB; D is a rational line; EF is the breadth from applying AB squared to D
EF = EG + GF where G divides EF into two parts corresponding to the two applied areas

configuration_map: The configuration consists solely of line segments: AB divided at C, rational line D, and result line EF divided at G. Point G lies between E and F, partitioning EF into EG (breadth of the rational area AC^2+CB^2 applied to D) and GF (breadth of the medial area 2*AC*CB applied to D). No triangles, circles, angles, or non-trivial spatial relationships are constructed. All reasoning is about commensurability relations (rational, medial, commensurable in square only) and algebraic identities.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing entirely with commensurability relations between line segments and areas (rational, medial, commensurable in length, commensurable in square only). It uses algebraic identities (2.4, 2.5) and proportional results (6.1, 10.11-10.15, 10.20-10.22) but constructs no geometric figures beyond simple line segment partitions. There are no angle decompositions, no points inside/outside figures, no ray orderings, no circle relationships — none of the spatial configuration patterns that could produce contradictions. This is a typical Book 10 algebraic proposition.
